questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Spoken language of the study destination, courses at the university, accommodation possibilities, cultural possibilities, climate of the destination

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find, but the system at the University in Cork was very different and more loose than what I am used to. This made it difficult to know whether the information was just non specific or if I missed some of it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to pay a lot for the student accommodation offered through the university even though it is off campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive, but also worth the money. Everything works, and you don't need to worry about anything at the accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very different from my own university and you didn't get a confirmation of your chosen courses until a week or something in to the semester.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everyone signed up through an online portal but this portal apparently did not work for law students. I had to write the information of the courses I wished to follow in an excel-file and send it to the responsible person at the university. Then the course would show up on Canvas, if I got a space on the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could contact the responsible person, and she was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: A few of the classes I wanted were not offered, but I found others.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be flexible in your wishes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level of the classes was very variable, but none of them seemed to exactly match the level at my own university.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Again, the level of the courses was not that high. This was the case for both the BA and MA courses I took.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more focused on lectures without student participation and on mandatory tutorials.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Environmental Law, International Human Rights Law, Legal Research and Writing, Introduction to Law of the Sea

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Environmental Law was very good. The lecturer was very interesting and knew a lot about the subject. A lot of other international students on the course as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: At my accommodation we had to bring everything for the kitchen so I had to by plates, cutlery etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive than in DK. Rent was more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything. There were so many clubs and societies you could join. They even said that if there was something missing, you could start your own society.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The mountaineering club was really good, but be prepared for the tickets selling out fast.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the west coast outside of the very touristy spots. Mizen head was really nice. Also Aran Islands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everyone was so nice and accommodating.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs and societies and spend time on campus

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People talk way more to strangers when at a pub or something than at home. If you went out with friends, you would most likely talk to others.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Rent is expensive, people are very nice, the weather is unpredictable - bring a raincoat.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The introduction at the university was very informative.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The traveling and the new friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out how everything worked.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
